ITQAN:v4p335/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p335/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p335/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interpreted “a remnant of knowledge” as astrology or divination (al-najāmah).
ITQAN:v4p335/r5.anchor: وأما النجامة ففي قوله ﴿ أو أثارة من علم ﴾ فقد فسره بذلك ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r7.claim: The idols people call on are challenged to identify anything they created on earth; the question rebukes them, and the interrogative is the second object of areaytum while also suspending arūnī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r7.anchor: قل أرأيتم ما تدعون: معناه أخبروني عن الذين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r8.claim: Arūnī may instead emphasize areaytum in the sense of tell me, with its second object omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r8.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون أروني توكيدا لأرأيتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows either a transitive construction with ما as its object or a nontransitive attention-getter followed by an admonitory question; Abu Hayyan prefers the object analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: يحتمل أرأيتم وجهين: أحدهما: أن تكون متعدية، وما مفعولة بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r2.claim: The phrase ماذا خلقوا من الأرض means either parts of the earth, whose creation belongs to God, or what is on its surface with an omitted noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه يريد من أجزاء الأرض، أي خلق ذلك إنما هو لله، أو يكون على حذف مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r3.claim: The demand for a prior book challenges idolaters because the Qur'an and all revealed books affirm divine oneness and refute associating partners with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r3.anchor: وكل كتب الله المنزلة ناطقة بذلك فطلب منهم أن يأتوا بكتاب واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r4.claim: أثارة can mean a remnant of knowledge, by analogy with a camel retaining some fat or a family retaining traces of old honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r4.anchor: أو أثارة من علم، أي بقية من علم، أي من علوم الأولين، من قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r5.speaker: الراعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r5.claim: Al-Ra'i's line uses أثارة for a remaining bit of fat, supporting that lexical sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r5.anchor: وذات أثارة أكلت علينا ... نباتا في أكمته قفارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r6.claim: The majority read أثارة as a verbal noun meaning a trace or remainder of something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أو أثارة، وهو مصدر، كالشجاعة والسماحة، وهي البقية من الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r7.claim: Al-Hasan interprets أثارة as knowledge that people extracted and then transmit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: المعنى: من علم استخرجتموه فتثيرونه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r8.claim: Mujahid takes the challenge to ask whether anyone can transmit knowledge about the idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المعنى: هل من أحد يأثر علما في ذلك؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r9.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains أثارة as an isnad or chain of transmission, supported by al-A'sha's line about a transmitter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p431/r9.anchor: وقال القرطبي: هو الإسناد، ومنه قول الأعشى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r1.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r1.claim: Abu Salama and Qatada interpret أثارة as special knowledge God has favored someone with, deriving it from أثرة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r1.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، وقتادة: المعنى: أو خاصة من علم، فاشتقاقها من الأثرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says أثارة is writing lines in the soil, an Arab divinatory practice; Abu Hayyan says this either lacks evidential force or, if accepted, mocks their claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المراد بالأثارة: الخط في التراب، وذلك شيء كانت العرب تفعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r3.claim: If Ibn Abbas's interpretation is sound, the verse sarcastically treats the diviners' practice as an argument for idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r3.anchor: كان ذلك من باب التهكم بهم وبأقوالهم ودلائلهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r4.speaker: علي، وابن عباس، وزيد بن علي، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والحسن، والسلمي، والأعمش، وعمرو بن ميمون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r4.claim: These readers have أثرة without the alif, a singular form whose plural is أثر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r4.anchor: أو أثرة بغير ألف، وهي واحدة، جمعها أثر كقترة وقتر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r5.speaker: علي، والسلمي، وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r5.claim: They also read أثرة with a still ث, meaning one transmitted report or trace that would suffice as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r5.anchor: وعلي، والسلمي، وقتادة أيضا: بإسكان الثاء ، وهي الفعلة الواحدة مما يؤثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r6.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i is reported to read with a damma on hamza and a still ث; Ibn Khalawayh also reports forms with hamza kasra or damma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p432/r6.anchor: وعن الكسائي: ضم الهمزة وإسكان الثاء.

STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r8.claim: The opening answers disbelievers, calls them to account for rejecting revelation, and affirms that revelation is not a human innovation.
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r8.anchor: Al-Aḥqāf begins with a response to the disbelievers, calling them to account for their rejection of the revelation and confirming the nature of revelation as something that is not a human innovation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r3.claim: Arab idolaters evade the warning because they rely on alleged deities and intercessors, imagining these beings can save them at Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r3.anchor: since they rely on their alleged deities and intercessors, they do not pay heed to the warnings of the Qur’ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r4.claim: The challenge asks whether the objects of worship created any part of earth or share in creating the heavens; without such a role they cannot be partners in God’s sovereignty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r4.anchor: they can only deserve to be called partners of God if they have any role in the creation of the heavens and the earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r5.claim: The argument relies on common ground: Arabian idolaters themselves acknowledged God as Creator of everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r5.anchor: the idolaters of Arabia regarded God to be the Creator of everything. Thus this argument is based on something which they too acknowledged

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r6.claim: The Arabic term athārah denotes an inherited tradition transmitted from forefathers, as defined in Aqrab al-mawārid.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p286/r6.anchor: refers to a tradition which is transmitted from someone’s forefathers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r1.claim: A claim that God has partners can be settled only by God’s own testimony, known through revelation or faithfully transmitted tradition; conjecture cannot justify it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r1.anchor: whether God has a partner or not is an issue which can only be resolved through God’s testimony

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r2.claim: Although the Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures suffered interpolations, neither they nor transmitted accounts of Abraham and earlier prophets contain evidence of polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r2.anchor: Though the Torah, the Gospel and other scriptures have been inflicted with large-scale interpolations yet they contain no trace of polytheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r3.claim: Arabian idolaters claimed ancestral precedent, but repeated Qur’anic challenges could not elicit any religious or rational basis for their practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r3.anchor: they were unable to prove if their ways had a religious or rational basis

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r4.claim: The verse’s qualifying words require inherited tradition to rest on knowledge rather than fancy or conjecture.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p287/r4.anchor: The words which qualify it are meant to show that this tradition should be based on knowledge and not on fancy or conjecture

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r1.claim: Al-Farra cites Abdullah's reading qul araytum man tadʿūna; araytum is a well-known Arabic form of the original araʾaytum, with another dialect softening the second hamza.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r1.anchor: لغة معروفة للعرب كثيرة ، وأرأيتم الأصل ، ولغة ثالثة

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r2.claim: The reading with mā follows the ordinary nonrational form for idols; man treats the worshipped idols as rational beings.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r2.anchor: جاء به على بابه لأنه للأصنام

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r3.speaker: القراء
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r3.claim: All readers agree on the masculine plural khalaqū and lahum, not the feminine or singular alternatives.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا أجمعت القراء على أن قرءوا

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r4.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reads aw atharah.

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r5.claim: Al-Farra reports a third dialect form, atharah with fatḥa on the hamza.

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r6.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i reports a fourth form, athārah with ḍamma on the hamza; he and al-Farra treat the forms as Arab usages with the same basic meaning.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r6.anchor: وحكى الكسائي لغة رابعة وهي أو أثرة بضم الهمزة والمعنى في اللغات الثلاث عند الفراء واحد

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra gives the sense as a remnant of knowledge or something transmitted from the books of earlier peoples; he analyzes athārah as a verbal noun and athrah as athar.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r7.anchor: والمعنى عنده بقية من علم ويجوز أن يكون المعنى عنده شيئا مأثورا من كتب الأولين

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r8.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r8.claim: Al-Kisa'i says the reported forms are all Arab usage and mean something transmitted.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r8.anchor: فأما الكسائي فإنه قال أثارة وأثرة وأثرة كل ذلك تقول العرب

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas explains the transmitted thing as something spoken about or reported, and relates the terms to athara and related roots.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ومعنى الشيء المأثور المتحدث به

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas says a soundly transmitted report has the Prophet forbidding oaths by fathers: swear by God or remain silent; Umar then says he never did so again, either from memory or by reporting another's oath.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r10.anchor: ومما صح سنده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سمع عمر وهو يقول وأبي

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r11.claim: Dhākiran means personally saying the oath, while āthiran means transmitting that someone else swore by it; the same root appears in maʾthūr reports.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r11.anchor: فقوله ذاكرا معناه متكلما بها وقائلا بها كما يقال ذكرت لفلان كذا

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r12.claim: The root also appears in expressions for raising dust and making something soft underfoot; mīthara reflects a wāw changed to yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r12.anchor: ومن هذا حديث مأثور يقال أثر الحديث يأثره وأثر يفعل ذلك

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r13.claim: The strongest explanation of the warning against swearing by other than God is that the swearer associates another with God in the supreme reverence that belongs only to God.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r13.anchor: وفي معنى قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حلف بغير الله جل وعز فقد أشرك أقوال أصحها أن المعنى

NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r14.claim: For the report's wording kufr, the strongest explanation is covering or concealing the reverence due to God.
NAHHAS:v4p157#3/r14.anchor: وفي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد كفر أقوال فمن أصحها أن الكفر هو التغطية

SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r1.claim: أرأيتم and أروني may reinforce one another because both mean “tell me”; then ما تدعون is the first object and ماذا خلقوا the second.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r1.anchor: أن تكون توكيدا لها لأنهما بمعنى أخبروني، وعلى هذا يكون المفعول الثاني ل " أرأيتم " قوله: " ماذا خلقوا "

SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r2.claim: If أروني is not emphatic, the verbs compete for a second object; ماذا خلقوا is shared, with the later verb governing and an object omitted from the earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r2.anchor: أن لا تكون مؤكدة لها، وعلى هذا تكون المسألة من باب التنازع

SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows أرأيتم to be intransitive and takes ما تدعون as an interrogative rebuke; تدعون means “worship.” Al-Samīn identifies this as al-Akhfash’s view, also used at 18:63.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r3.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية في " أرأيتم " أن لا يتعدى. وجعل " ما تدعون " استفهاما معناه التوبيخ.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r4.claim: من الأرض explains the ambiguity in ماذا خلقوا.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r4.anchor: " من الأرض " هذا بيان الإبهام الذي في قوله: " ماذا خلقوا ".

SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4/r5.claim: أم here is disconnected, and شرك means participation or partnership.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes من قبل هذا as an adjective of كتاب, supplying “a revealed book from before this.”
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r1.anchor: صفة ل " كتاب " أي: بكتاب منزل من قبل هذا. كذا قدره أبو البقاء.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r2.claim: Al-Samīn prefers a more general implied word: “something existing from before this.”
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r2.anchor: كون مطلق أي: كائن من قبل هذا.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r3.claim: The common reading أثارة is a verbal noun on فعالة, like سماحة, غواية, ضلالة, meaning a remnant.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r3.anchor: العامة على " أثارة " وهي مصدر على فعالة كالسماحة والغواية والضلالة، ومعناها البقية

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r4.claim: A camel idiom describes an animal that was fat, grew lean leaving a remnant of fat, then became fat again.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r4.anchor: إذا كانت سمينة ثم هزلت، وبقيت بقية من شحمها ثم سمنت.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r5.claim: أثارة is especially used for a remnant of honor or nobility, but also more broadly; al-Rāʿī’s line witnesses it.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r5.anchor: والأثارة غلب استعمالها في بقية الشرف. يقال: لفلان أثارة أي: بقية أشراف، ويستعمل في غير ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r6.speaker: عمر
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r6.claim: A derivation connects أثارة to أثر, “transmit”; ʿUmar’s saying means without remembering it or transmitting it from another.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r6.anchor: قول عمر: " ما حلفت ذاكرا ولا آثرا " أي: مسندا له عن غيري.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses الآثر for someone who reports or transmits.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r7.anchor: وقال الأعشى: 4039أ إن الذي فيه تماريتما

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r8.speaker: علي وابن عباس وزيد بن علي وعكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r8.claim: These readers and others read أثرة without alif: a singular form whose plural is أثر, like قترة/قتر.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن عباس وزيد بن علي وعكرمة في آخرين " أثرة " دون ألف، وهي الواحدة. ويجمع على أثر كقترة وقتر.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r9.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads أثرة and إثرة, with ḍamma or kasra on hamza and a still thāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي " أثرة " و " إثرة " بضم الهمزة وكسرها مع سكون الثاء.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r10.speaker: قتادة والسلمي
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r10.claim: Qatāda and al-Sulamī read أثرة with fatḥa on hamza and a still thāʾ; it means a single transmitted report.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r10.anchor: وقتادة والسلمي بالفتح والسكون. والمعنى: بما يؤثر ويروى. أي: ايتوني بخبر واحد يشهد بصحة قولكم.

SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r11.claim: Demanding just one report is a concessive challenge, since claimants are known to lie; من علم is an adjective of أثارة.
SAMIN-DURR:46:4#2/r11.anchor: وهذا على سبيل التنزل للعلم بكذب المدعي. و " من علم " صفة لأثارة.

ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r3.claim: An alternate reading drops the alif in araytum.
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r3.anchor: ويقرأ أريتم بغير ألف. (ما تدعون من دون الله)

ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r4.claim: The objects invoked besides God are things the people claim to be deities.
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r4.anchor: ما تدعونه إلها من دون الله. (أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك

ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r5.claim: The challenge asks whether idols shared in creating the heavens, which would justify worshipping them alongside God.
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r5.anchor: أي في خلق السماوات، أي فلذلك أشركتموهم في عبادة الله عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r6.claim: The challengers are asked for an earlier revealed book proving their claims about the idols.
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r6.anchor: أي ايتوني بكتاب أنزل فيه برهان ما تدعون.

ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r7.claim: Variants are athārah, atharah, and athrah with quiescent thāʾ; the phrase may mean a mark, a remnant, or transmitted knowledge.
ZAJJAJ:v4p437/r7.anchor: ويقرأ (أو أثارة من علم)، وقرئت أو أثرة من علم - بإسكان الثاء - ومعناها؛ إذا قال: أثارة على معنى علامة من علم

ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r1.claim: The challengers of polytheism must show what the beings invoked besides God created on earth or whether they shared in making the heavens.
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r1.anchor: Show me what these [beings or forces) have created anywhere on earth! Or had they, perchance, a share in [creating] the heavens?

ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r2.claim: He demands an earlier divine writ or any vestige of knowledge to substantiate their claim.
ASAD-NOTES:46:4/r2.anchor: bring me any divine writ preceding this one, or any [other] vestige of knowledge

ASAD-NOTES:46:4#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:4#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:4#n4/r1.claim: The demanded evidence would support the claim that divine powers exist besides God.
ASAD-NOTES:46:4#n4/r1.anchor: in support of your claim that there are other divine powers besides God

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r1.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r1.claim: Al-Khuli was a pioneering hermeneuticist in Arabic and, as far as the author knows, perhaps across the Islamic world.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r1.anchor: إن الخولي هو أول هرمنيوطيقي بالعربية، وربما في عالَم الإسلام

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r2.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r2.claim: Al-Khuli's approach studies how the interpreter thinks and projects a worldview, culture, and understanding onto the verses; this is a starting point for renewing tafsir.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r2.anchor: أن المنحى الذي يدعو إليه أمين الخولي في تفسير القرآن يهتم بالتعرف على الطريقة التي يفكر بها المفسر، وكيف يُسقط المفسر رؤيتَه للعالَم وثقافته وفهمه

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r3.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r3.claim: Al-Khuli rejects contemporary tafsir used merely as a tool for sectarian choices and advocacy, however important those aims may be.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r3.anchor: ليس مقبولًا عند الخولي أن يظل التفسير المعاصِر مجرد أداةٍ لاختياراتٍ مذهبيةٍ وتوظيفاتٍ دعويةٍ مهما كانت أهميتُها

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r4.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r4.claim: Reading Al-Khuli's response to the Encyclopedia of Islam article on tafsir, the author found an alternative horizon and method for interpreting and construing the Quran with new tools borrowed from German hermeneutics.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r4.anchor: وجدتُه يتحدث عن أفقٍ مختلف ومنهجٍ بديل لتفسير النص القرآني وتأويلِه، في ضوء أدواتٍ ومفاهيم جديدة

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r5.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r5.claim: Al-Khuli served as imam at the Egyptian legation in Rome and later Berlin; after returning from Germany in 1927, he taught at Al-Azhar. The author surmises his German stay exposed him to hermeneutics.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r5.anchor: وعند عودته من ألمانيا سنة ١٩٢٧م باشر التدريس في الأزهر. ويبدو أن مكوثَه في ألمانيا أتاح له فرصة التعرف على الهرمنيوطيقا

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r6.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r6.claim: Modern hermeneutics originated in Germany: Schleiermacher shaped its modern concept in the late eighteenth century, developed by Dilthey and Heidegger and brought to its height by Gadamer.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r6.anchor: فمع شلايرماخر نهاية القرن الثامن عشر تبلور مفهومٌ مختلفٌ للهرمنيوطيقا في العصر الحديث، وتطور هذا المفهوم مع وليم دلتي، ومارتن هيدغر

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r7.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r7.claim: German philosophy has remained a reference for hermeneutic thought in the Islamic world.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r7.anchor: كانت وما زالت الفلسفة الألمانية مرجعية التفكير الهرمنيوطيقي في عالم الإسلام

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r8.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r8.claim: About forty years after Al-Khuli, cleric Mohammad Mojtahed Shabestari went to Germany, learned hermeneutics in German while imam in Hamburg, then returned to Iran to promote and explain it in Persian.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r8.anchor: الشيخ محمد مجتهد شبستري، الذي ذهب إلى ألمانيا، بعد رحلة الشيخ أمين الخولي بأربعين عامًا تقريبًا، فعمل إمامًا للمركز الإسلامي في هامبورغ، وتعلم الهرمنيوطيقا بالألمانية هناك

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r9.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r9.claim: The author argues religious thought should be rebuilt by clergy first because they know the tradition, recognize the urgent need, and care about religious thought's future.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r9.anchor: إعادة بناء الفكر الديني تتطلب أن ينهض بها رجال الدين قبل غيرهم؛ لأنهم الأكثر دراية بالتراث

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r10.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r10.claim: The author parallels these clerical exchanges with Rifa'a al-Tahtawi, a cleric who introduced Arab readers to Western achievements through his book after serving as imam to an Egyptian student mission in Paris.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r10.anchor: تعرفت العربية على ملامح من صورة الغرب وتقدمه عبر كتاب «تخليص الإبريز في تلخيص باريز»

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r11.claim: Al-Khuli did not explain when or how he encountered hermeneutics, and the writings the author consulted do not clarify it, despite modern scholars' accounts of his pioneering role and disciples.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r11.anchor: لم يتحدث الخولي عن المرحلة والكيفية التي تعرف بها على الهرمنيوطيقا، ولم تخبرنا الكتابات التي اطلعنا عليها بما يوضح ذلك

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r12.speaker: السيد أحمد خليل
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r12.claim: Ahmad Khalil identifies Schleiermacher's influence on Al-Khuli and notes that the factors Al-Khuli adopted for interpretation were the same ones Schleiermacher had earlier emphasized.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r12.anchor: ما كتبه السيد أحمد خليل من تأثير شلايرماخر على الخولي، وتبنيه للنهج الجديد الذي اختطه شلايرماخر في تعريف عملية التفسير بوصفها «فنًّا للفهم»

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r13.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r13.claim: The author says Al-Khuli's works, especially his discussion of tafsir, convinced him of this reading, and Ahmad Khalil's account strengthened that conviction.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r13.anchor: وأقنعتني مطالعة آثاره بذلك، خاصةً ما تحدث فيها عن التفسير، وعزز قناعتي ما كتبه السيد أحمد خليل

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r14.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r14.claim: The author thinks Al-Khuli's engagement stopped with Schleiermacher and nineteenth-century followers, without deeper engagement with philosophical hermeneutics, whether by choice or circumstance.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r14.anchor: ويبدو لي أن اطلاع الخولي توقف عند شلايرماخر وأتباعِه في القرن التاسع عشر، ولم يشأ، أو لم تسمح له ظروفُه

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r15.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r15.claim: In Heidegger and Gadamer, philosophical hermeneutics treats interpretation as an ontological event encompassing texts and existence.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r15.anchor: الهرمنيوطيقا الفلسفية، الذي أضحت عملية التفسير على وفقها: «حدثًا أنطولوجيًّا»، يتسِع للنصوص والوجود أيضًا، كما شرحها هيدغر وتلميذُه غادامير

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r16.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r16.claim: Al-Khuli's horizon of the interpreter makes interpretation an active dialogue and reciprocal production of meaning between interpreter and text, rather than passive reception.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r16.anchor: بل أصبح التفسير في رأي الخولي عملية حوارٍ وإنتاجٍ متبادَل للمعنى، يشترك فيها المفسر مع النص

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r17.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r17.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r17.claim: Modern hermeneutics is an art of understanding that examines how interpreters receive texts and produce meaning in light of their expectations, worldview, culture, assumptions, and preconceptions.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r17.anchor: قراءةً للقراءة، أو فهمًا للفهم، أو تفسيرًا لكيفية تلقي المفسر للنص، وطريقة إنتاجه للمعنى المقتنَص منه، في ضوء: أفق انتظارِه، ورؤيتِه للعالم

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r18.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r18.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r18.claim: Later Arabic hermeneutic writing mainly applied the method to literary and other texts as a tool of literary criticism.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r18.anchor: غير أنها انشغلت بتطبيقاتِها على النصوص الأدبية وغيرها، وتوظيفِها أداةً في النقد الأدبي

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r19.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r19.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r19.claim: Hermeneutics experts in the Islamic world warn against applying it to Quranic and religious texts, fearing hostility from clergy attached to traditional tafsir and anxious about new methods.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r19.anchor: كل الخبراء بالهرمنيوطيقا في عالَم الإسلام يحذرون من تطبيقِها في تفسير القرآن، وتوظيفها في فهم النصوص الدينية

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r20.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r20.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r20.claim: Al-Khuli boldly pioneered this work early, introducing hermeneutics and directing his students to apply it to Quranic interpretation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r20.anchor: لم ينفرد بريادتِه للكتابة والتعريف بهذا الفن فقط، بل بادر أيضًا لتوجيه تلامذتِه لتطبيقِه على تفسير القرآن

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r21.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r21.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r21.claim: Al-Khuli formed a literary and hermeneutic studies group with Muhammad Ahmad Khalafallah, Aisha Abd al-Rahman (Bint al-Shati), and Muhammad al-Alai, known as al-Umana.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r21.anchor: مثل محمد أحمد خلف الله، وعائشة عبد الرحمن «بنت الشاطئ»

RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r22.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r22.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r22.claim: Al-Khuli also advocated opening tafsir to sociology, psychology, and modern human sciences to build a different method of understanding and interpretation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c5/r22.anchor: بل رأى ضرورة الانفتاح على علم الاجتماع وعلمِ النفس والعلوم الإنسانية الحديثة، لأجل بناء منهج مختلف للفهم والتفسير

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r3.claim: Judgment is certain, and polytheism and intercession provide no rational or revealed basis for ignoring its warning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r3.anchor: there is nothing in reason and revelation to support such superstitions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r4.claim: The Qur’an’s message was foretold by a great Israelite witness, with its predictions also found in the Torah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r4.anchor: by a great witness belonging to the Israelites and something whose predictions are mentioned in the Torah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r5.claim: The opponents should not be misled by Jewish and Christian support, since those communities deny their own messengers and scriptures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r5.anchor: these people are denying their own messengers and scriptures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r11.claim: The opponents trust deities and intercessors to save them at Judgment, although neither reason nor revelation supports that confidence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p281/r11.anchor: These people trust their deities and intercessors; they reckon that if ever the Day of Judgement comes, they will save them

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة وعمرو بن ميمون والأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās (with variant transmission), ʿIkrima, Qatāda, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, and reportedly al-Aʿmash read أو أثرة من علم without alif.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن عباس -بخلاف- وعكرمة وقتادة وعمرو بن ميمون، ورويت عن الأعمش:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r2.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r2.claim: ʿAlī and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read أثرة with still thāʾ.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي "عليه السلام" وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي: "أو أثرة"، ساكنة الثاء.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r3.claim: The common أثارة/أثارة means a remnant or transmitted trace, from أثر الحديث; a مأثور sword bears marks of workmanship. The still-thāʾ أثرة is stronger, asking for just one report or isolated account as proof.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p264/r3.anchor: الأثرة والأثارة التي تقرأ2 بها العامة: البقية، وما يؤثر.

QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#1/r1.speaker: Cs
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#1/r1.claim: Cs's mutawātir reading deletes hamza, simplifying raʾā to raytum in a common Ḥijāzī practice.
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza deletion — raʾā simplified to raytum, common Ḥijāzī practice

QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#2/r1.claim: The hmz mutawātir reading softens hamza, producing an intermediate form between full hamza and deletion.
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#2/r1.anchor: Hamza softening — intermediate between full hamza and deletion

QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#3/r1.speaker: madd
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#3/r1.claim: The madd mutawātir reading lengthens the vowel before hamza, giving the word a deliberative prosody.
QIRAAT-ER:46:4:2#3/r1.anchor: Madd extension — lengthened vowel before hamza creates deliberative prosody

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains an athāra as a trace or thing extracted and brought to light.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r1.anchor: عن من سمع الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ أو أثارة من علم ﴾ قال أثرة شيء يستخرجه فيثيره

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r2.claim: Qatāda offers the alternative sense of a particular or privileged item of knowledge.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة أو خاصة من علم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r3.claim: Asked about divinatory line drawing, the Prophet says it was knowledge taught to a prophet; a line is valid only if it matches that knowledge.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r3.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الخط

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the reported knowledge of line drawing as an athāra, a surviving trace of knowledge.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p215/r4.anchor: قال صفوان فحدثت به أبا سلمة بن عبد الرحمن فقال أبو سلمة حدثت به ابن عباس فقال هو أثرة من علم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r1.claim: The command to say this rebukes and reproaches the polytheists.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r4.claim: ما تدعون means “what you worship besides God.”
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r4.anchor: ما تعبدون ( من دون الله ( من الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r5.claim: The objects of worship may be idols or all false deities; al-Alusi says the broader reading is more apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r5.anchor: جميع المعبودات الباطلة ولعله الأظهر والموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r6.claim: The relative ما is the first object of أرأيتم; أروني repeats it for emphasis and also means “tell me.”
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r6.anchor: والموصول مفعول أول لأرأيتم وقوله تعالى : ( أروني (

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r7.claim: Al-Alusi gives three parses: interrogative ما with redundant ذا; ماذا as one interrogative object; or interrogative ما with relative ذا, whose clause is خلقوا.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r7.anchor: و ( ذا ) زائدة وأن تكون ( ماذا ) اسما واحدا مفعولا مقدما

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r8.claim: On the first two parses, خلقوا is the second object of أرأيتم; on the other parses, the whole ماذا خلقوا clause is its second object.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r8.anchor: وعلى الأولين جملة ( خلقوا ) مفعول ثان لأرأيتم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan allows the two verbs to compete in government, with the later verb governing and the earlier one's object omitted; al-Alusi records his choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r9.anchor: وقد أعمل الثاني وحذف مفعول الأول واختاره أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r10.claim: Another analysis makes أروني an appositive of inclusion to أرأيتم.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya offers a transitive أرأيتم with ما as object, or a nontransitive attention-getter with interrogative ما for rebuke; al-Akhfash gives the latter for 18:63.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r12.claim: The phrase مِنَ الْأَرْضِ explains what the question ماذا خلقوا refers to.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r13.claim: Earth may mean its parts and regions, its surface creatures and other things with an implied noun, or the lower worlds generally; al-Alusi prefers the last.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r13.anchor: أجزاء الأرض وبقعها وجوز أن يكون المراد ما على وجهها

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r14.claim: Their alleged شرك is a share with God in creating the heavens, understood as the upper worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r14.anchor: شركة مع الله سبحانه ( في السماوات ( أي في خلقها

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r15.claim: أم may be disconnected or connected.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r15.anchor: جوز أن تكون منقطعة وأن تكون متصلة والمراد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r16.claim: The challenge denies that idols independently created any lower-world part and then denies that they shared in creating the upper world; either denial removes any claim to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r16.anchor: فقد نفي أولا مدخليتها في خلق شيء من أجزاء العالم السفلي حقيقة واستقلالا

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r17.claim: The wording singles out the heavens because that is the obvious point conceded by everyone, while apparent human agency in lower-world events is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5/r17.anchor: إلزامهم بما هو مسلم لهم ظاهر لكل أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r1.claim: The demand for a book taunts them by showing they cannot produce transmitted evidence, after the challenge to produce rational evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r1.anchor: بتعجيزهم عن الإيمان بسند نقلي بعد تبكيتهم بالتعجيز عن الإتيان بسند علقي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r2.claim: They are asked for a prior divine book, before the Quran, supporting the truth of their religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r2.anchor: بكتاب إلهي كائن ( من قبل هذا ( الكتاب أي القرآن الناطق بالتوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r3.claim: أثارة can mean a remnant of ancient knowledge left to them that supports their claim; it is a verbal noun like ضلالة.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r3.anchor: بقية من علم بقيت عليكم من علوم الأولين

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r4.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains أثارة as an isnad or narration, supported by al-A'sha's use of الآثر for the transmitter.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r4.anchor: وقال القرطبي : هي بمعنى الإسناد والرواية ومنه قول الأعشى

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r5.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن، قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r5.claim: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman and Qatada say it means a special piece of knowledge God selected for its holder.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة : المعنى أو خاصة من علم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r6.claim: Another explanation takes أثارة to mean a sign.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r7.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r7.claim: A report through Ibn Abbas, also reported mawquf from him, has the Prophet explain أثارة as writing.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ( أو أثارة من علم ) قال : الخط

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r8.claim: A marfu report from Abu Hurayra says a prophet used to draw a line and whoever matched it knew; al-Alusi relates this to geomancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r8.anchor: حديث أبي هريرة مرفوعا وكان نبي من الأنبياء يخط فمن صادف

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r9.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r9.claim: Al-Bahr suggests that, if Ibn Abbas's interpretation as writing in sand is sound, it taunts the polytheists and their arguments.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r9.anchor: إن صح تفسير ابن عباس الأثارة بالخط في التراب كان ذلك من باب التهكم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r10.claim: The tanwin signals a small amount, and مِنْ عِلْمٍ modifies أثارة: a little remnant of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r10.anchor: والتنوين للتقليل و ( من علم ) صفة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r11.claim: Their claim cannot stand without rational proof or transmitted evidence; neither supports them, while both support the contrary, proving their claim false.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r11.anchor: ما لم يقم عليها برهان عقلي أو دليل نقلي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r12.claim: A reading with kasra on the hamza is explained as a thing that reveals or stirs meanings, metaphorically like dust raised by horsemen in debate.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r12.anchor: بالمنظرة فإنها تثير المعاني وقيل : وذلك من باب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r13.speaker: علي، ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r13.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas read أثرة without the alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r13.anchor: بخلاف عنهما وزيد بن علي وعكرمة وقتادة والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r14.speaker: زيد بن علي، عكرمة، قتادة، الحسن، السلمي، الأعمش، عمرو بن ميمون
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r14.claim: Zayd ibn Ali, Ikrima, Qatada, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, al-A'mash, and Amr ibn Maymun also read أثرة without the alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r14.anchor: زيد بن علي وعكرمة وقتادة والحسن والسلمي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r15.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r15.claim: Al-Kisai is also reported to read with damma on the hamza and still tha, a measure or any small amount of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r15.anchor: وعن الكسائي ضم الهمزة وإسكان الثاء فهي اسم للمقدار كالغرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r16.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r16.claim: Another reading attributed to al-Kisai has kasra on the hamza and still tha, with the same meaning as أثرة.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r16.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أنه قرأ ( إثرة ) بكسر الهمزة وسكون الثاء

ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r17.speaker: غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r17.claim: One view supplies an omitted counterpart to connected أم: do they have a share in earth, or a share in heaven?
ALUSI-FULL:v26p5#2/r17.anchor: قيل : الأظهر أن تجعل الآية من حذف معادل ( أم ) المتصلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r1.claim: The challenge asks idolaters to produce a scripture sent by God before the Quran that supports their claims about their idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r1.anchor: ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا} أي بكتاب جاءكم من الله قبل القرآن فيه بيان ما تقولون،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi explains athara as a remainder of knowledge transmitted from earlier people and attributed to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r2.anchor: {أو أثارة من علم} قال الكلبي: أي بقية من علم يؤثر عن الأولين، أي يسند إليهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r3.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, and Muqatil explain it as a report transmitted from prophets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وعكرمة ومقاتل: رواية عن الأنبياء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r4.claim: Qatada interprets it as a special kind of knowledge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r5.claim: The word derives from athar, a transmitted report; athartu al-hadith athran or atharatan means I transmitted the report.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p249#3/r5.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من الأثر وهو الرواية، يقال: أثرت الحديث أثرا وأثارة، ومنه قيل للخبر: أثر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r6.claim: The challenge asks whether their gods contributed to creating any part of the world such that they merit worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r6.anchor: هل يعقل أن يكون لها في أنفسها مدخل في خلق شيء

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r7.claim: Mentioning partnership in the heavens guards against imagining that intermediaries share in producing earthly events.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r7.anchor: أي أخبروني عن حال آلهتكم بعد تأمل فيها، هل يعقل

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r8.claim: They must produce a scripture predating the Quran that affirms God's oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r8.anchor: من قبل هذا الكتاب يعني القرآن فإنه ناطق بالتوحيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r9.claim: Alternatively, they must produce ancient learning supporting their gods' right to worship or a command to worship them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r9.anchor: أو بقية من علم بقيت عليكم من علوم الأولين

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r10.claim: The challenge first denies rational grounds for their gods and then denies transmitted proof.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r10.anchor: نقلا بعد إلزامهم بعدم ما يقتضيها عقلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r11.claim: إثارة with kasra can mean debate that stirs meanings; أثرة may mean something selected or passed down, with three hamza vowels explained by derivation and usage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:1-4/r11.anchor: أي مناظرة فإن المناظرة تثير المعاني

BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links al-Aḥqāf to al-Jāthiyah: after the prior sūrah's rebuke of deniers, it records their wrongdoing and painful return, proceeds from creation's signs to idol worship and their rejection of clear signs, then coheres through the end.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير رحمه الله تعالى : لما قدم ذكر الكتاب وعظيم الرحمة به وجليل بيانه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r2.claim: Since they claimed to be intelligent and called idols partners, the argument reasons that a sensible person prepares against a warning, and only an equal or stronger partner could protect them; it begins by dismantling that claim.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r2.anchor: ولما قرر سبحانه الأصل الدال على التوحيد وإثبات العدل والحرمة بالبعث للفصل , وكانوا يقولون : إنهم أعقل الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r3.claim: The command exposes their folly in risking harm without protection: they have neither rational nor transmitted proof that their idols are divine, a rank that requires decisive evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p116/r3.anchor: بأنهم أعرضوا عما قد يضرهم من غير احتراز منه دالا على عدم إلهية ما دعوه آلهة بعدم الدليل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r1.claim: “Besides God” means beneath the supreme King, who has no equal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r1.anchor: { من دون الله } أي الملك الأعظم الذي كل شيء دونه , فلا كفوء له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r2.claim: Since seeing the idols is already obvious, the question is construed as asking about their status: are they partners in the earth? The following “show me” begins a fresh challenge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r2.anchor: ولما كان من المعلوم أن الاستفهام عن رؤية ما مشاهدتهم له معلومة لا يصح إلى بتأويل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r3.claim: The challenge asks what the idols created in the earth that could substantiate their claimed partnership there.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r3.anchor: { أروني ما } وأكد الكلام بقوله سبحانه وتعالى : { ماذا خلقوا } أي اخترعوه { من الأرض } ليصح ادعاء أنهم شركاء فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r4.claim: The parallel challenge asks whether the idols share in the heavens through governance, as naturalists claim, creation, or any other kind of partnership.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r4.anchor: { أم لهم } أي الذين تدعونهم { شرك في السماوات } أ ] نوع من أنواع الشركة : تدبير - كما يقول أهل الطبائع , أو خلق أو غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r5.claim: The verse uses “ḥadhf by counterpart” (iḥtibāk): mentioning creation first implies its omission in the second clause, while partnership in the second implies its omission in the first.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r5.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الخلق أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا , والشركة ثانية دليلا على حذفها أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r6.claim: Because proof can be transmitted or rational, the challenge demands evidence that the idols created anything or deserve worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r6.anchor: ولما كان الدليل أحد شيئين : سمع وعقل , قال تعالى : { ائتوني } أي حجة على دعواكم في هذه الأصنام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r7.claim: The earlier books meant include the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms; all attest God's oneness, so citing them would expose the idolaters' claim and is a sign of prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r7.anchor: أي الذي نزل علي كالتوراة والإنجيل والزبور , وهذا من أعلام النبوة فإنها كلها شاهدة بالوحدانية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r8.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r8.claim: Ibn Burjān explains athārah as a remaining trace of something after it has disappeared, inherited from predecessors and preserved in their accounts.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r8.anchor: قال ابن برجان : وهي البقية من أثر كل شيء يرى بعد ذهابه وحال رؤيته بأثرها خلق عن سلف يتحدثون بها في آثارهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r9.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r9.claim: Al-Baghawī says athārah derives from athar, meaning a transmitted report.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r9.anchor: قال البغوي : وأصل الكلمة من الأثر وهو الرواية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r10.claim: Any fragment of knowledge that supports their claim counts, whether based on necessity, experiment, observation, another source, or even conjecture.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r10.anchor: { من علم } أي قطعي بضرورة أو تجربة أو مشاهدة أو غيره ولو ظنا يدل على ما ادعيتم فيهم من الشركة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r11.claim: If they cannot produce evidence, the challenge rebukes them as liars, especially since they abhor and regard lying as vile.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p117/r11.anchor: ولما كان لهم من النفرة من الكذب واستشناعه واستبشاعه واستفظاظه ما ليس لأمة من الأمم , أشار إلى تقريعهم بالكذب

DURR-FULL:v7p434/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Shabi, explains athārah as fine handwriting.
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r1.anchor: من طريق الشعبي عن ابن عباس {أو أثارة من علم} قال: جودة الخط

DURR-FULL:v7p434/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says it may mean lines Arabs used to draw on the ground.
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r2.anchor: من طريق أبي سلمة عن ابن عباس في قوله {أو أثارة من علم} قال: خط كان تخطه العرب في الأرض

DURR-FULL:v7p434/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r3.claim: Qatada glosses it as a special portion of knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {أو أثارة من علم} قال: أو خاصة من علم

DURR-FULL:v7p434/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as clear proof of the matter.
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أو أثارة من علم} يقول: بينة من الأمر

DURR-FULL:v7p434/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r5.claim: Mujahid explains it as someone transmitting knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v7p434/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أو أثارة من علم} قال: أحد يأثر علما

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r1.claim: Al-Ahqaf is Meccan and has thirty-five verses.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها خمس وثلاثون مقدمة سورة الأحقاف

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Ahqaf was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت بمكة سورة {حم} الأحقاف

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr likewise reports that al-Ahqaf was revealed in Mecca.

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, reporting from the Prophet, glosses athārah min ʿilm as line-writing; another report from him gives the same gloss.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم {أو أثارة من علم} قال: الخط

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r8.claim: The Prophet says a prophet knew line-drawing, and whoever matches his line knows it.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r8.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الخط فقال: علمه نبي

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r9.claim: The Prophet says one of the prophets used to draw lines; whoever matches his line knows.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط

DURR-FULL:v7p433/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r10.claim: Abu Said glosses the phrase as good handwriting.
DURR-FULL:v7p433/r10.anchor: عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {أو أثارة من علم} قال: حسن خط

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas quoting the Prophet glosses “a trace of knowledge” as divination by lines.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r1.anchor: من طريق أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن ، عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أو اثارة من علم قال : ' الخط '

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains “a trace of knowledge” as clear evidence about the matter.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3293/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أو اثارة من علم يقول : بينة من الامر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r1.claim: The command to come is metaphorical for producing evidence, even if the evidence is already in the disputants’ presence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r1.anchor: والإتيان مستعار للإحضار ولو كان في مجلسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r2.claim: This refers to a book predating the Qur’an, already present in their minds because it is repeatedly recited to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r2.anchor: إلى القرآن لأنه حاضر في أذهان أصحاب المحاجة فإنه يقرأ عليهم معاودة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r3.claim: Requiring an earlier book blocks them from composing a text for the challenge, as they claimed they could produce something like the Qur’an themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r3.anchor: ووجه تخصيص الكتاب بوصف أن يكون من قبل القرآن ليسد عليهم باب المعارضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r4.claim: Athāra, with fatḥa on the hamza, means a remnant: a report preserved from earlier learned people though not written in a book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r4.anchor: و { أثارة } بفتح الهمزة : البقية من الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r5.claim: Expanding the kinds of admissible evidence makes their inability to supply any of it a more decisive refutation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r5.anchor: وهذا توسيع عليهم في أنواع الحجة ليكون عجزهم عن الإتيان بشيء من ذلك أقطع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r6.claim: The challenge presses and silences them: they have no proof from reason or transmitted sources, whether written or oral.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p11/r6.anchor: وفي قوله : { إن كنتم صادقين } إلهاب وإفحام لهم بأنهم غير آتين بحجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r9.claim: Araytum may be transitive with ma as object, or intransitive as an attention-getter with ma a reproachful question.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: قل أرأيتم يحتمل أرأيتم وجهين: أحدهما أن تكون متعدية، وما مفعولة بها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r10.anchor: تعبدون. قال الفراء: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r11.claim: Al-Farra reports that Abd Allah ibn Masud's reading is من تدعون instead of ما تدعون.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: «قل أرأيتم من تدعون» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r12.claim: Min is partitive, since everything on the earth's surface, including animals, is from the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: من الأرض، من، للتبعيض، لأن كل ما على وجه الأرض من حيوان ونحوه فهو من الأرض.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r13.claim: The challenge asks whether idols share in the heavens, then demands an earlier revealed book prescribing idol worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r13.anchor: ثم وقفهم على السماوات هل لهم فيها شرك، ثم استدعى منهم كتابا منزلا قبل القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r14.claim: Athara may mean an ancient remnant of a scholar's knowledge supporting idol worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r14.anchor: وقوله: أو أثارة معناه: أو بقية قديمة من علم أحد العلماء يقتضي عبادة الأصنام.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r15.claim: Most readers have athara as a verbal noun like courage or generosity; it means a remainder or trace.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p91#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «أو أثارة» على المصدر، كالشجاعة والسماحة، وهي البقية من الشيء كأنها أثره.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r1.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r1.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan understands it as knowledge someone draws out and brings to light.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r1.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: المعنى من علم تستخرجونه فتثيرونه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r2.claim: Mujahid asks whether anyone transmits such knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المعنى هل من أحد يأثر علما في ذلك.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r3.speaker: القرظي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r3.claim: Al-Qurazi says athara means an isnad; al-Asha's line uses athir for a transmitter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r3.anchor: وقال القرظي: هو الإسناد، ومن هذا المعنى قول الأعشى: [السريع]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r4.claim: Umar's saying فما خلفنا بها ذاكرا ولا آثرا illustrates athir as a transmitter or reported trace.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r4.anchor: آثرا أي للسند عن غيره، ومنه قول عمر رضي الله عنه: فما خلفنا بها ذاكرا ولا آثرا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r5.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r5.claim: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman and Qatada understand it as a special portion of knowledge God singled out its holder to possess.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r5.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة: المعنى وخاصة من علم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن العباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says athara means lines in the ground, which Arabs used for divination and omens.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r6.anchor: المراد ب «الأثارة» : الخط في التراب، وذلك شيء كانت العرب تفعله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r7.claim: Asked about ground-drawing, the Prophet reportedly said a prophet used to draw lines and whoever matched his line had it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r7.anchor: وروي أن النبي عليه السلام سئل عن ذلك فقال: «كان نبي من الأنبياء يخطه، فمن وافق خطه فذاك»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r8.claim: The report's apparent sense supports ground-drawing as valid if someone matches the prophet's line; many scholars read it this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r8.anchor: وظاهر الحديث تقوية أمر الخط في التراب، وأنه شيء له وجه إذا وفق أحد إليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r9.claim: Another group takes the report as rejecting the practice: it belonged to a departed prophet whose revelation ended, and ordinary people cannot match his line.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل معناه الإنكار، أي أنه كان من فعل نبي قد ذهب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r10.claim: Athara can mean a remnant of old nobility, as when a family has ancient signs of honor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r10.anchor: كانت عندهم شواهد قديمة، وتستعمل في غير ذلك، ومنه قول الراعي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r11.speaker: الراعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r11.claim: Al-Rai's poem uses athara for the remnant of fat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r11.anchor: وذات أثارة أكلت عليه ... نباتا في أكمتها قصارى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r12.speaker: عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r12.claim: Al-Sulami reads أثرة without alif; this form is also reported from Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ikrima, Amr ibn Maymun, and al-A'mash.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r12.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن السلمي فيما حكى الطبري: «أو أثرة» بفتح الهمزة والثاء والراء دون ألف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r13.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r13.claim: Al-Thalabi reports Ikrima's reading ميراث من علم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r14.claim: Ali and al-Sulami are reported with a quiescent thāʾ, a single transmitted item sufficient as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r14.anchor: بسكون الثاء وهي الفعلة الواحدة مما يؤثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r15.claim: A group reads أثرة with a damma on hamza and a quiescent thāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r15.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: «أثرة» بضم الهمزة وسكون الثاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r16.claim: These readings can all mean: do you have knowledge God singled out and favored you with?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p92/r16.anchor: وهذه كلها بمعنى: هل عندكم شيء خصكم الله به من علم وآثركم به.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r1.claim: The opening of the verse was explained at Fatir 40 through the phrase “bring me a book.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r1.anchor: مفسر في فاطر 40 إلى قوله ﴿ ائتوني بكتاب ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r2.claim: The verse omits an implied challenge: if they claim their gods made something, produce a pre-Quran book proving that the idols are God's partners.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r2.anchor: فقل لهم إيتوني بكتاب ﴿ من قبل هذا ﴾ أي من قبل القرآن فيه برهان ما تدعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says athāra is something its extractor brings out.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه الشيء يثيره مستخرجه قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة والفراء وأبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba, al-Farra, and Abu Ubayda take it as a remnant of knowledge preserved from earlier people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r4.anchor: بقية من علم تؤثر عن الأولين قاله ابن قتيبة وإلى نحوه ذهب الفراء وأبو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets it as a sign or mark of knowledge.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو رزين وأيوب السختياني ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r6.claim: Ibn Masud, Abu Razin, Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, and Ya'qub read atharah with fatḥa on the thāʾ, like shajarah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو رزين وأيوب السختياني ويعقوب أثرة بفتح الثاء مثل شجرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says this reading means a line that Arabs used to draw on the ground; Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash identifies the line as divination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه الخط قاله ابن عباس وقال هو خط كانت العرب تخطه في الأرض قال أبو بكر بن عياش الخط هو العيافة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r8.claim: Mujahid says it means knowledge transmitted from others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r8.anchor: أو علم تأثرونه عن غيركم قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r9.claim: Qatada says it means a special kind of knowledge.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r10.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Ya'mar read athrah with a still thāʾ and no alif, on the pattern nazrah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن يعمر أثرة بسكون الثاء من غير ألف بوزن نظرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r11.claim: Al-Farra treats athārah and athrah as dialect forms meaning a remnant of knowledge, possibly something transmitted from earlier books; he explains the forms as verbal nouns built on different patterns.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r11.anchor: وقال الفراء قرئت أثارة وأثره وهي لغات ومعنى الكل بقية من علم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r12.speaker: اليزيدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r12.claim: Al-Yazidi says athārah is a remnant, while athrah is the verbal noun of transmitting or recounting, as in ma'thur report.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p369/r12.anchor: وقال اليزيدي الأثارة البقية والأثرة مصدر أثره يأثره أي يذكره ويرويه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r4.claim: The idols created no part of earth and share nothing in the heavens; all ownership and control belong to God, so the pagans have no warrant for worshipping them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r4.anchor: أي: ولا شرك لهم في السموات ولا في الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r5.claim: The challenge asks for a revealed book commanding idol worship or a clear proof for this practice; the pagans have no transmitted or rational evidence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r5.anchor: هاتوا كتابا من كتب الله المنزلة على الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r6.claim: Other readers pronounce the word أثرة; Ibn Kathir explains this reading as sound knowledge faithfully transmitted from someone before them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses atharah as someone who transmits knowledge.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains atharah as a clear proof or indication of the matter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r8.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: أو بينة من الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r9.claim: Ahmad reports Ibn Abbas interpreting atharah as writing or line-drawing; Sufyan says he is unsure whether Ibn Abbas heard this from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال سفيان: لا أعلم إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r10.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r10.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says atharah means a remnant of knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن عياش: أو بقية من علم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r11.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri explains atharah as something extracted and brought to light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p274#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: {أو أثارة} شيء يستخرجه فيثيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو بكر بن عياش
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also explain atharah as writing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو بكر بن عياش أيضا: {أو أثارة من علم} يعني الخط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r2.claim: Qatada explains atharah as a particular or special part of knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: {أو أثارة من علم} خاصة من علم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says these glosses are close and return to his explanation of atharah as clear proof; he notes Ibn Jarir chose this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p275/r3.anchor: وكل هذه الأقوال متقاربة، وهي راجعة إلى ما قلناه، وهو اختيار ابن جرير

BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r1.claim: The command 'say' addresses the unbelievers as a rebuke and a confutation.

BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r3.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols, celestial bodies, and other objects of worship.
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r3.anchor: ما تعبدون {من دون الله} من الأصنام والكواكب

BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r4.claim: The command 'show me' reinforces the preceding 'tell me.'

BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r5.claim: Mādhā clarifies the ambiguous question: which part of earth did the supposed gods create independently of God? 'What you worship' is the first object of arāʾaytum, and 'what they created' its second; together they ask about the gods' state.
BURSEVI:v8p358#2/r5.anchor: أي جزء من أجزاء الأرض تفردوا بخلقه دون الله

BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r1.claim: Their alleged partnership with God would have to extend to creating, possessing, or governing the heavens to give them any plausible claim to worship; one with no role in anything's existence has no such claim, especially an inanimate idol.
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r1.anchor: شركة مع الله تعالى. {فى السماوات} ؛ أي : في خلقها

BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r2.claim: Although Jesus revived the dead, created a bird, and performed extraordinary acts, he did so by God's power and permission; this does not deny his own incapacity.
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r2.anchor: فإنه كان يحيي الموتى ويخلق الطير

BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r3.claim: The verse names the upper heavens because their elevated, unsupported structure makes God's exclusive creation especially evident; alternatively, it avoids suggesting celestial intermediaries share in producing earthly events.
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r3.anchor: لأن الآثار العلوية أظهر دلالة على اختصاص الله تعالى بخلقها

BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r4.claim: Bursevī prefers a connected interrogative with an omitted counterpart: 'Do they have a share in earth, or in heaven?' This is the stronger parsing noted in Ḥawāshī Saʿdī al-Muftī.
BURSEVI:v8p358#3/r4.anchor: من حذف معادل ، أم المتصلة لوجود دليله

BURSEVI:v8p359/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r1.claim: The demand for a book rebukes the idolaters by showing they cannot supply transmitted proof, after the preceding challenge showed they cannot supply rational proof; the preposition conveys bringing a divine book.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r1.anchor: تبكيت لهم بتعجيزهم عن الإتيان بسند نقلي بعد تبكيتهم بالتعجيز عن الإتيان بسند عقلي

BURSEVI:v8p359/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r2.claim: They are challenged to produce a scripture predating the Qur'an that validates their religion, but all revealed scriptures affirm the Qur'an's monotheism and refutation of associationism.

BURSEVI:v8p359/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r3.claim: Athāra is a remnant of earlier knowledge that might testify to the idols' entitlement to worship; Arab usage compares it to a camel fattened on a remnant of meat and fat.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r3.anchor: بقية كائنة من علم بقيت عليكم من علوم الأولين شاهدة باستحقاقهم للعبادة

BURSEVI:v8p359/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r4.claim: A claim needs rational or transmitted proof; the idolaters have neither, while both kinds of evidence disprove it, so their claim is false.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r4.anchor: لا تكاد تصح ما لم يقم عليها برهان عقلي أو نقلي

BURSEVI:v8p359/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r5.claim: The cited Persian couplet ridicules any claimant to partnership in God's realm: no other master has dominion over His creation.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r5.anchor: واحد اندر ملك اورا يارنى بنكانش را جزا وسالارنى نيست خلقش

BURSEVI:v8p359/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r6.claim: Inwardly, idols such as ego and Satan cannot act in the earth of the self or heavens of the spirit; God alone creates and turns hearts toward truth or error.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن كل ما يعبد من دون الله من الهوى والشيطان

BURSEVI:v8p359/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p359/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p359/r7.claim: Outer and inner scholars agree on sincere worship; serving for reward or fear of punishment still regards other than God, so true worship seeks neither paradise nor Hell.
BURSEVI:v8p359/r7.anchor: اتفق العلماء من أهل الظاهر والباطن على وجوب الإخلاص حتى قالوا

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports a Prophetic promise of ten good deeds per grain of sand for reciting al-Aḥqāf, ten sins erased, and ten ranks raised; no grading is stated.
