JISHUMI:v9p6395/r2.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب أن النبي - صلى الله عليه قال: من قرأ سورة (الأحقاف) أعطي من الأجر بعدد كل رمل

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r4.claim: The common reading is qul araʾaytum, as in the regional codices.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: قل أرأيتم وهي كذلك في مصاحف الأمصار

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r5.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd has qul araʾaytkum.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: قل أرأيتكم

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r6.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r6.claim: The common reading has athāra with an alif.

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is reported to read athara without alif, with fatḥa on the hamza.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r7.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب - رضي الله عنه -: أو أثرة بفتح الهمزة

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r8.claim: Athāra may mean transmitted evidence; ʿIkrima glosses it as an inheritance of knowledge.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r8.anchor: والثاني على ما يؤثر، وقيل: فصل من آثر يؤثر إيثارا، وعن عكرمة: أو ميراث من علم

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r9.claim: Athāra derives from athar, a transmitted report.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r9.anchor: والأثارة: أصلها من الأثر، وهو الرواية

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r10.speaker: الأعشى
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r10.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line is cited as evidence for a transmitted report.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r10.anchor: قال الأعشى: إن الذي فيه تماريتما

JISHUMI:v9p6395/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r11.speaker: الراعي
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r11.claim: Al-Rāʿī's line supports athāra as a remnant or remainder.
JISHUMI:v9p6395/r11.anchor: والأثارة، والأثر: البقية أيضا، يقال: بهذه الناقة أثارة من سمن، أي: بقية من سمن، قال الراعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r9.speaker: الحسن وطائفة معه
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a group read athara as athrah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r9.anchor: قرأ الحسن وطائفة معه { أو أثرة }

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r10.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r10.claim: On the majority reading, athāra means a report of knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r11.claim: Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh says it means a remnant, as in a poem about remnant fat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r11.anchor: بقية , قاله أبو بكر بن عياش , ومنه قول الشاعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r12.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r12.claim: Mujāhid says it is knowledge inherited from others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r12.anchor: أو علم تأثرونه عن غيركم , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r13.claim: It may mean effort or reasoning based on knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r13.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أو اجتهاد بعلم , لأن أثارة العلم الاجتهاد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r14.claim: It may also mean argument based on knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r14.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : أو مناظرة بعلم لأن المناظر في العلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r15.claim: For athrah, Ibn ʿAbbās transmits from the Prophet the meaning ‘writing.’
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r15.anchor: أنه الخط , وقد رواه ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r16.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r16.claim: ʿIkrima says it means inherited knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r17.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r17.claim: Qatāda says it means special knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r18.speaker: عطية
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r18.claim: ʿAṭiyya says it means a remnant of knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r18.anchor: أو بقية من علم ، قاله عطية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r19.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p270/r19.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it is something extracted and brought forth.

MUJAHID:v2p593/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p593/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p593/r1.claim: Mujahid explains this as someone who transmits knowledge.
MUJAHID:v2p593/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أو أثارة من علم ﴾ قال يقول أو أحد يأثر علما

MUQATIL:46:4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:4/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:4/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to address Mecca's people; the deities they worship besides God are identified here as angels.
MUQATIL:46:4/r1.anchor: يا محمد لأهل مكة { أرأيتم ما تدعون } يعني تعبدون { من دون الله } من الآلهة، يعني الملائكة

MUQATIL:46:4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:4/r2.claim: The challenge asks what these alleged gods created of the earth, as God created it, if they are truly gods.
MUQATIL:46:4/r2.anchor: يعني الأرض كخلق الله إن كانوا آلهة

MUQATIL:46:4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:4/r3.claim: The question challenges their claim to a share in heaven's dominion and is linked to the statement that they have no share in the heavens or earth.
MUQATIL:46:4/r3.anchor: ثم قال: { أم لهم } يقول: ألهم { شرك } من الله { في } ملك { السماوات } كقوله:

MUQATIL:46:4/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:4/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:4/r4.claim: The disbelievers are challenged to produce an earlier scripture or transmitted prophetic report affirming that God has a partner.
MUQATIL:46:4/r4.anchor: من الأنبياء قبل هذا القرآن بأن له شريكا

MUQATIL:46:4/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:4/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:4/r5.claim: The alleged partners in the Meccans' claim are al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat.
MUQATIL:46:4/r5.anchor: يعني اللات والعزى ومناة بأنهن له شركاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ قل أرأيتم ﴾ أخبروني ﴿ ما تدعون من دون الله ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r2.claim: What they call upon besides God are the idols they worship.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r3.claim: The challenge asks what, among things on earth, the idols created, if they are truly gods.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r3.anchor: أي شيء خلقوا مما في الأرض إن كانوا آلهة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r4.claim: The question asks whether they share with God in creating the heavens and earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r4.anchor: شركة مع الله في خلق السموات والأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r5.claim: The Qur'an declares monotheism and invalidates idolatry, as do all earlier revealed scriptures; they are challenged to produce one earlier book that supports worshipping other than God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r5.anchor: أي من قبل هذا الكتاب وهو القرآن يعنى أن هذا الكتاب ناطق بالتوحيد وأبطال الشرك وما من كتاب أنزل من قبله من كتب الله إلا وهو ناطق بمثل ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r6.claim: Athārah means a remnant of knowledge inherited from the ancients.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p135#4/r6.anchor: أو بقية عليكم علم بقيت عليكم من علوم الأولين

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r1.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols and rivals the polytheists worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r1.anchor: أي ما تعبدون من الأصنام والأنداد من دون الله

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r2.claim: The challenge asks whether the idols created anything at all from the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r2.anchor: أي هل خلقوا شيئا من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r3.claim: Shirk here means a share in creating the heavens alongside God.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r3.anchor: أي نصيب { في السماوات } أي في خلق السموات مع الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r4.claim: The requested earlier book would be one that came before this Qur'an.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r5.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r5.claim: The common reading is athārah, with an alif after the thāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet explained athārah as lines Arabs used to trace on the ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r6.anchor: هو خط كانت تخطه العرب في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi judged the Ibn Abbas report about geomantic lines unsound.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the line report is established through Muawiya ibn al-Hakam in Muslim and gives another sound route from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r8.anchor: قلت: هو ثابت من حديث معاوية بن الحكم السلمي خرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r9.claim: The separate report that a prophet drew lines and that a matching line is accurate is also said here to be unsound.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r9.anchor: كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط فمن وافق خطه فذاك

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r10.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports one view that line divination is permitted because a prophet practiced it, and another that it is forbidden because its prophetic method cannot be identified.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r10.anchor: جاء لإباحة الضرب لأن بعض الأنبياء كان يفعله.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r11.claim: Al-Qurtubi adopts the prohibition: line divination derives guesses from planetary figures, claims inaccessible unseen knowledge, and seeking it is sinful or unbelief according to intent.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4/r11.anchor: ترجع إلى صور الكواكب، فيدل ما يخرج منها على ما تدل عليه تلك الكواكب

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r1.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r1.claim: Al-Khattabi reads the matching-line hadith as a warning: line reading was a prophetic sign whose practice ended with that prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r1.anchor: قوله عليه السلام: «فمن وافق خطه فذاك»

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r2.speaker: القاضي عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r2.claim: Qadi Iyad says the wording appears to affirm the successful match, but coincidence cannot be known and the law forbids divination and claims to the unseen; it grants no permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r2.anchor: لكن من أين تعلم الموافقة والشرع منع من التخرص وادعاء الغيب جملة

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r3.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r3.claim: Makki says the prophet who drew lines used his index and middle fingers in sand and then performed divination.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r3.anchor: وحكى مكي في تفسير قوله: «كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط» أنه كان يخط بأصبعه السبابة والوسطى

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a geomancer paid to draw quick lines in soft earth, erase them two at a time, and infer success from two remaining or failure from one; Arabs called it al-asham.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r4.anchor: هو الخط الذي يخطه الحازي فيعطى حلوانا فيقول: اقعد حتى أخط لك

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi allows dreams as a sign of the unseen because they are part of prophethood, and permits good-omen interpretation while prohibiting omens and divinatory augury.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r5.anchor: إن الله تعالى لم يبق من الأسباب الدالة على الغيب التي أذن في التعلق بها والاستدلال منها إلا الرؤيا فإنه أذن فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r6.claim: Faʾl is taking encouragement from good words heard about a planned matter; one should proceed happily, while ignoring unpleasant words rather than turning back.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r6.anchor: والفأل: هو الاستدلال بما يسمع من الكلام على ما يريد من الأمر إذا كان حسنا

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r7.claim: The Prophet prayed that there is no omen except God's omen, no good except God's good, and no deity besides Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r7.anchor: اللهم لا طير إلا طيرك ولا خير إلا خيرك ولا إله غيرك

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi accepts the poet's condemnation of divination and soothsaying but rejects including faʾl, which the law expressly exempts and commends.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r8.anchor: وهذا كلام صحيح، إلا في الفأل فإن الشرع استثناه وأمر به

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r9.claim: God alone knows the unseen except where He informs someone or gives a customary sign; such signs are defeasible, as date-palm flowering may fail or fruit may grow again after apparent loss.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r9.anchor: أن الله سبحانه منفرد بعلم الغيب، وأن أحدا لا يعلم ذلك إلا ما أعلمه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r10.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r10.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says athārah means handwriting and reports that Malik initially ruled by handwriting when the writer was recognized.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#2/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أو أثارة من علم } يريد الخط. وقد كان مالك رحمه الله يحكم بالخط

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r1.claim: Malik later reversed judgment by handwriting after fraud and forgery spread, saying that people's corruption brings new rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r1.anchor: ثم رجع عن ذلك حين ظهر في الناس ما ظهر من الحيل والتزوير.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r2.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r2.claim: Ibn Khuwayz says Malik's school permits judgment when witnesses authenticate a judge's letter or a will as handwriting even if they do not know its contents, and likewise a person's written admission of debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r2.anchor: فأما إذا شهد الشهود على الخط المحكوم به مثل أن يشهدوا أن هذا خط الحاكم وكتابه،

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي وأبو بكر بن عياش
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, and others interpret athārah as a remnant of knowledge, as do the lexicons.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: «أو أثارة من علم» أو بقية من علم قاله ابن عباس والكلبي وأبو بكر بن عياش

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r4.claim: Athārah and atharah can mean a remaining portion, as in camels fattening on leftover fat; al-Raʿi's verse illustrates the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r4.anchor: سمنت الإبل على أثارة أي بقية شحم كان قبل ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r5.speaker: ميمون بن مهران وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r5.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran, Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, and Qatada take athārah to mean a special portion of knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r5.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن وقتادة: «أو أثارة من علم» خاصة من علم.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r6.claim: Mujahid interprets it as a report transmitted from people who came before.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: رواية تأثرونها عمن كان قبلكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r7.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r7.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil understand it as a report passed down from prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومقاتل: رواية عن الأنبياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r8.speaker: القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurazi says it means an isnad, or chain of transmission.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reads it as something that is brought forth or extracted.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r9.anchor: الحسن: المعنى شيء يثار أو يستخرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r10.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says athārah means a sign; it is a verbal noun like generosity or bravery, from the root for a trace or transmitted report.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «أو أثارة» أي علامة. والأثارة مصدر كالسماحة والشجاعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r11.claim: Athar, athārah, and atharah can mean relating a report from someone else; a maʾthūr hadith is transmitted generation to generation with a sound chain.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r11.anchor: ومنه قيل: حديث مأثور أي نقله خلف عن سلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r12.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r12.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line about what is clear to the listener and transmitter is cited as evidence for the sense of transmitted report.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r12.anchor:
قال الأعشى: إن الذي فيه تماريتما
بين للسامع والآثر

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r13.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r13.claim: A reading has u as the vowel of the hamza and a silent thāʾ in athrah; it can mean a remainder of knowledge or something inherited from earlier books.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r14.speaker: السلمي والحسن وأبو رجاء
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r14.claim: Al-Sulami, al-Hasan, and Abu Raja read atharah with a fatḥah on hamza and thāʾ, without the alif, meaning special knowledge granted or preferred to its holders.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r14.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والحسن وأبو رجاء بفتح الهمزة والثاء من غير ألف

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r15.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r15.claim: Another report gives al-Hasan's reading atharah with open hamza and silent thāʾ; Ikrima explains it as an inheritance of knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r15.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أيضا وطائفة «أثرة» مفتوحة الألف ساكنة الثاء

QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r16.claim: The verse lays out the forms of proof: rational argument that inert idols neither harm nor benefit, then transmitted proof from an earlier book or inherited knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:46:4#3/r16.anchor: فيه بيان مسالك الأدلة بأسرها فأولها المعقول،

QASHANI:46:3-6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:46:3-6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:46:3-6/r4.claim: Calling upon others besides God means naming them and ascribing existence or causal power to them; the challenge asks what they created or affected independently in earth or jointly in heaven.
QASHANI:46:3-6/r4.anchor: تسمونه وتثبتون له وجودا وتأثير أي شيء كان

QASHANI:46:3-6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:46:3-6/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:46:3-6/r5.claim: The requested evidence could be transmitted from an earlier scripture or rational proof grounded in sound knowledge.
QASHANI:46:3-6/r5.anchor: على ذلك بدليل نقلي من كتاب سابق أو عقلي من علم متقن

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r1.claim: The objects invoked besides God are idols.

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r2.claim: The idols neither created any part of the world nor assisted the Creator in any part of it; reason rules out both claims, even for the smallest thing.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r2.anchor: هل يعقل أن يضاف إليها خلق جزء من أجزاء هذا العالم

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r3.claim: Since God alone is the true Creator and benefactor, worship, the highest form of reverence, is due only to Him, the source of the greatest beneficence.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r3.anchor: والعبادة عبارة عن الإتيان بأكمل وجوه التعظيم ، وذلك لا يليق إلا بمن صدر عنه أكمل وجوه الإنعام

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r4.claim: If idol worship is defended as obedience to God's command, that command can only be established through revelation or transmitted prophetic teaching, so the opponents must produce evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r4.anchor: بقي أن يقال إنا لا نعبدها لأنها تستحق هذه العبادة ، بل إنما نعبدها لأجل أن الإلاه الخالق المنعم أمرنا بعبادتها

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r5.claim: Rāzī dismisses a command to worship idols in revelation to Muhammad as plainly false.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r5.anchor: أما إثبات ذلك بالوحي إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو معلوم البطلان

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r6.claim: Earlier revealed scriptures all prohibit idol worship, a fact established by necessary, widely transmitted knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r6.anchor: لأنه علم بالتواتر الضروري إطباق جميع الكتب الإلاهية على المنع من عبادة الأصنام

RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r7.claim: No transmitted prophetic teaching outside the scriptures calls people to worship idols; therefore idol worship is baseless and false.
RAZI-FULL:v28p4#2/r7.anchor: لأن العلم الضروري حاصل بأن أحدا من الأنبياء ما دعا إلى عبادة الأصنام

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r1.claim: This is among several challenges for disbelievers to produce evidence verifying their claims.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r1.anchor: This is one of several verses that challenge the disbelievers to bring something to verify their claims

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r2.claim: Those invoked apart from God are idols or beings such as jinn whom idolaters treat as partners.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r2.anchor: That which you call upon apart from God means idols or beings such as jinn whom the idolaters treat as partners with God

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r3.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r3.claim: The requested book means a revealed scripture.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r3.anchor: Bring me a book is a request that they bring a revealed scripture (Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r4.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r4.claim: One interpretation of a vestige of knowledge is a remnant of teachings from earlier people.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r4.anchor: some vestige of knowledge means some remnant from the teachings of those of old (Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r5.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r5.claim: Another interpretation is something written by people before.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r5.anchor: Others interpret vestige of knowledge to mean something that was written by those before (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r6.claim: A further interpretation is any authentic report transmitted from earlier sources.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r6.anchor: though it is also understood to mean any authentic report that has been transmitted (R)

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r7.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r7.claim: Every interpretation asks for evidence establishing the idols’ and jinn’s alleged partnership with God.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r7.anchor: something that indicates the veracity of the idolaters’ claim that these idols and jinn whom they worship are indeed partners with God (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:46:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r8.claim: Elsewhere the Quran asks whether God gave them a book on whose clear proof they stand.
STUDYQURAN:46:4/r8.anchor: or did We give them a book, such that they stand upon a clear proof from it? (35:40; cf. 34:44; 43:21; 68:37–38)

QUSHAYRI:v3p194/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p194/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p194/r5.claim: The challenge asks whether idols have any effect in dominion or power to benefit and harm; if worshipers have proof, they should produce it, and otherwise abandon error.
QUSHAYRI:v3p194/r5.anchor: أي أثر فيهم في الملك ، أو القدرة على النفع والضر

TAB-FULL:v21p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p112/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p112/r1.claim: The idols created nothing of the earth; God created the whole earth from nothing, and His creation supports worshipping Him alone.
TAB-FULL:v21p112/r1.anchor: فإن ربي خلق الأرض كلها، فدعوتموها من أجل خلقها ما خلقت من ذلك آلهة وأربابا

TAB-FULL:v21p112#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p112#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p112#3/r1.claim: The challengers must produce an earlier divine book proving their idols created anything or share in the heavens; such a share would entail gratitude and service, though only God can create.
TAB-FULL:v21p112#3/r1.anchor: لأن ذلك لا يقدر أن يخلقه إلا الله

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r1.speaker: قراء الحجاز والعراق
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r1.claim: The Hijaz and Iraq readers generally read أثارة with alif, understood as a remainder of knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «خط كان يخطه العرب في الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r2.claim: Al-Sulami read أثرة without alif, meaning special knowledge granted to and preferred for its possessors.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «خط كان يخطه العرب في الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains أثارة as a line Arabs used to draw on the ground.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «خط كان يخطه العرب في الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r4.claim: Ibn Ayyash identifies the line-drawing as divination.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر: يعني ابن عياش: " الخط: هو العيافة "

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r5.claim: Qatada interprets أثارة as a special body of knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «أو خاصة من علم»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r6.claim: Al-Hasan understands it as something brought out through divination.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «أثارة شيء يستخرجونه فطرة»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses it as someone transmitting knowledge from another person.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، { أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «أحد يأثر علما»

TAB-FULL:v21p113/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r8.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses it as clear proof of the matter.
TAB-FULL:v21p113/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أو أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] يقول: «ببينة من الأمر»

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r1.claim: Ibn Ayyash also explains أثارة as a remainder of knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r1.anchor: سئل أبو بكر يعني ابن عياش عن، {أثارة من علم} [الأحقاف: 4] قال: «بقية من علم»

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r2.claim: The author prefers remainder of knowledge because it is the established Arabic sense; أثارة is a verbal noun from athara, patterned like سماجة and قباحة.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r2.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: الأثارة: البقية من علم، لأن ذلك هو المعروف من كلام العرب

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r3.speaker: راعي الإبل
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r3.claim: The poet's phrase ذات أثارة means a she-camel with some fat remaining, supporting the sense remainder.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r3.anchor: كما قال راعي الإبل: وذات أثارة أكلت عليها … نباتا في أكمته قفارا يعني: وذات بقية من شحم

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r4.claim: The variant أثرة derives from athar, meaning a trace, as in the forms قترة and غبرة.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r4.anchor: جعله أثرة من الأثر، كما قيل: قترة وغبرة

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r5.claim: A further reported reading has أثرة with a still thāʾ, compared to رجفة and خطفة.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأه «أو أثرة» بسكون الثاء، مثل الرجفة والخطفة

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r6.claim: A remainder of knowledge could be a trace of divination, knowledge recovered from earlier books, or special knowledge granted to some people.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r6.anchor: جاز أن تكون تلك البقية من علم الخط، ومن علم استثير من كتب الأولين، ومن خاصة علم كانوا أوثروا به

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r7.claim: Al-Tabari notes a report that the Prophet interpreted the word as line-drawing, promising to cite it later.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r7.anchor: وقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ذلك خبر بأنه تأوله أنه بمعنى الخط

TAB-FULL:v21p115/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r8.claim: The verse demands an earlier book or remnant of knowledge proving the idolaters' claims; a claim without evidence benefits no claimant.
TAB-FULL:v21p115/r8.anchor: {إن كنتم صادقين} [البقرة: 23] في دعواكم لها ما تدعون، فإن الدعوى إذا لم يكن معها حجة لم تغن عن المدعي شيئا

TABATABAI:46:3-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r1.claim: The sūrah warns polytheists who reject God and His Messenger of painful punishment for denying the Resurrection; it opens with proof of Resurrection and returns to it repeatedly.
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r1.anchor: إنذار المشركين الرادين للدعوة إلى الإيمان بالله ورسوله بالمعاد بما فيه من أليم العذاب

TABATABAI:46:3-10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r3.claim: The sūrah also argues for divine unity and prophethood, recalls ʿĀd and towns around Mecca, and tells of jinn who heard the Quran, believed, and returned to warn their people.
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r3.anchor: وإنباء عن حضور نفر من الجن عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم واستماعهم القرآن وإيمانهم به

TABATABAI:46:3-10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r4.claim: The sūrah is Meccan except two disputed verses to be identified in the later report section.
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r4.anchor: والسورة مكية كلها إلا آيتين اختلف فيهما سنشير إليهما في البحث الروائي الآتي

TABATABAI:46:3-10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r9.claim: Arāʾaytum means ‘tell me’; the objects invoked are the idols worshipped by the polytheists.
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r9.anchor: بمعنى أخبروني والمراد بما تدعون من دون الله الأصنام التي كانوا يدعونها ويعبدونها

TABATABAI:46:3-10/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r10.claim: Rational pronouns are used of the idols because worshippers attribute rational acts to them; the argument applies to every deity worshipped besides God.
TABATABAI:46:3-10/r10.anchor: لكونهم ينسبون إليه أفعال أولي العقل وحجة الآية وما بعدها مع ذلك تجري في كل إله معبود من دون الله

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r1.claim: Arūnī means ‘inform me’; mā is interrogative, dhā is extra, the whole phrase is the object of ‘created,’ and min al-arḍ attaches to it.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r1.anchor: و { ما } اسم استفهام و { ذا } بعده زائدة والمجموع مفعول { خلقوا } ومن الأرض متعلق به

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r2.claim: Having a share in the heavens means sharing in their creation, which is the matter under question.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r2.anchor: فإن خلق شيء من السماوات والأرض هو المسؤول عنه

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r3.claim: Though polytheists assigned their idols governance but creation to God, a share in governance entails a share in creation; there is no governance without creation.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r3.anchor: لما كان الخلق لا ينفك عن التدبير أوجب ذلك أن يكون لمن له سهم من التدبير سهم في الخلق

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r4.claim: The challenge asks what share their gods have in creating earth or heaven, since cosmic governance without creation is meaningless.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r4.anchor: فلا معنى للتدبير في الكون من غير خلق

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r5.claim: ‘This’ is the Quran; an earlier heavenly book such as the Torah would need to say their idols share in creation.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r5.anchor: كتاب سماوي كالتوراة نازل من عند الله يذكر شركة آلهتهم في خلق السماوات أو الأرض

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r6.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib explains athāra as transmission or narration of knowledge, originally following a trace.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r6.anchor: مصدر بمعنى النقل والرواية قال وأثرت العلم رويته

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r7.claim: On al-Rāghib's account it is a transmitted piece of knowledge proving the idols' share; most exegetes say ‘remnant,’ close to inherited knowledge.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r7.anchor: شيء منقول من علم يثبت أن لآلهتهم شركة

TABATABAI:46:4-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r8.claim: If truthful, they must produce a prior heavenly book, transmitted knowledge, or inherited remnant proving their gods shared in creating heaven or earth.
TABATABAI:46:4-5/r8.anchor: أو بقية من علم أورثتموها يثبت ذلك إن كنتم صادقين في دعواكم

TABRISI:46:1-5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r1.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وابن عباس وعكرمة وقتادة
TABRISI:46:1-5/r1.claim: Ali and al-Sulami read atharah with a still th; Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Qatada are reported with another vocalization; the common reading is itharah with an alif.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r1.anchor: قرأ علي ع وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي أو أثرة بسكون الثاء من غير ألف وقرأ ابن عباس بخلاف وعكرمة وقتادة أو أثرة بفتحتين

TABRISI:46:1-5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r2.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:46:1-5/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni says atharah and itharah mean a remnant or trace, as in transmitted speech, an artifact, or a sword bearing a mark of workmanship; singular atharah is stronger because it asks for even one rare piece of proof.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r2.anchor: قال ابن جني: الأثرة والإثارة البقية وهي ما يؤثر من قولهم أثر الحديث

TABRISI:46:1-5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:1-5/r7.claim: The idols created nothing on earth to merit worship and gratitude, nor do they share in creating or determining the heavens.

TABRISI:46:1-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:1-5/r8.claim: They are challenged to produce an earlier scripture that supports their claim about idols.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r8.anchor: القرآن أنزله الله يدل على صحة قولكم

TABRISI:46:1-5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:1-5/r9.claim: One gloss is a remnant of knowledge preserved from earlier books that says idols are God's partners.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r9.anchor: أي بقية من علم يؤثر من كتب الأولين يعلمون به أنهم شركاء الله

TABRISI:46:1-5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r10.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
TABRISI:46:1-5/r10.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil explain it as a report from earlier prophets.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r10.anchor: وقيل: أو أثارة من علم أي خبر من الأنبياء عن عكرمة ومقاتل

TABRISI:46:1-5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:46:1-5/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as a written line, meaning a written book.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو الخط أي بكتاب مكتوب عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:46:1-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r12.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:46:1-5/r12.claim: Qatada says it is a particular piece of knowledge reserved for you.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r12.anchor: وقيل: خاصة من علم أوثرتم بها عن قتادة

TABRISI:46:1-5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:1-5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:1-5/r13.claim: The challenge demands one of three proofs: reason, scripture, or transmitted report; lacking all three makes their claim false.
TABRISI:46:1-5/r13.anchor: والمعنى فهاتوا إحدى هذه الحجج الثلاث أولاها دليل العقل والثانية الكتاب والثالثة الخبر المتواتر

FARRA:v3p49/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p49/r1.claim: Although the referents are idols, the masculine plural verb treats them like people because they are imagined speaking, worshipping, and being honored like rulers.
FARRA:v3p49/r1.anchor: ثم قال: أروني ماذا خلقوا (4) ولم يقل: خلقت، ولا خلقن لأنه إنما أراد الأصنام، فجعل فعلهم كفعل الناس وأشباههم

FARRA:v3p49/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
FARRA:v3p49/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Masud reads من تعبدون, explicitly using a personal pronoun and human-like verb for the idols.
FARRA:v3p49/r2.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله [بن مسعود] : من تعبدون من دون الله، فجعلها (من) ، فهذا تصريح بشبه الناس في الفعل وفي الاسم.

FARRA:v3p49/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r3.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p49/r3.claim: Abdullah’s reading has أريتكم; he generally reads God’s forms أريت and أريتم with the kaf, as in أريتك الذي يكذب بالدين.
FARRA:v3p49/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : أريتكم، وعامة ما في قراءته من قول الله أريت، وأريتم فهي في قراءة عبد الله بالكاف

FARRA:v3p49/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وبعض القراء
FARRA:v3p49/r4.claim: Common readers have أثارة; some read أثرة, which Abu Abd al-Rahman read as Farra recalls, and another reported reading is أثره.
FARRA:v3p49/r4.anchor: قرأها العوام: «أثارة» ، وقرأها بعضهم قال: قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن فيما أعلم و «أثرة» خفيفة. وقد ذكر عن بعض القراء «أثره» .

FARRA:v3p49/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p49/r5.claim: All three forms mean a remnant of knowledge or something transmitted from books of earlier peoples.
FARRA:v3p49/r5.anchor: والمعنى فيهن كلهن: بقية من علم، أو شيء مأثور من كتب الأولين.

FARRA:v3p49/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p49/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p49/r6.claim: أثارة is a verbal noun like السماحة; أثرة is built on أثر like قترة; the other أثرة is analogized to خطفة and رجفة.
FARRA:v3p49/r6.anchor: فمن قرأ «أثارة» فهو كالمصدر مثل قولك : السماحة، والشجاعة. ومن قرأ «أثرة» فإنه بناه على الأثر، كما قيل: قترة .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#6/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi says the opening challenge is explained in the parallel passage at Fatir 35:40.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#6/r1.anchor: {قل أرأيتم} وهي مفسرة في سورة فاطر [آية:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r1.claim: The challenge asks for an earlier scripture that proves the claimed legitimacy of worshiping idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r1.anchor: {ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا} أي: ائتوني بكتاب من قبل القرآن فيه برهان ما تدعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Farra, and al-Zajjaj explain athāra as a remnant; Ibn Qutayba specifies a remnant of knowledge from earlier people, and al-Hasan relates it to something stirred up and extracted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: أي بقية، ويقال: ناقة ذات أثارة، أي بقية من شحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r3.claim: Al-Farra also allows athāra to mean something transmitted from the books of earlier peoples, and treats the form as a verbal noun like generosity or bravery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r3.anchor: وزاد الفراء فقال: ويقال أو شيء مأثور من كتب الأولين، قال: وأثارة على المصدر مثل: السماحة والشجاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives athāra the sense of a sign of knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r4.anchor: وزاد الزجاج فقال: (أثارة) معناها علامة من علم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives athāra from transmitted knowledge, the source of the term āthār for reports; he also records a sense of something beautiful to the eye, like a full attractive camel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r5.anchor: وقال المبرد: أثارة ما يؤثر من علم، كقولك: هذا حديث يؤثر عن فلان، ومن ثم سميت الأخبار الآثار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r6.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi groups the lexical explanations into three: a remnant, a transmitted report, or a mark/sign; the second sense is illustrated by al-Aʿsha's line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r6.anchor: وهو ينقسم إلى أقوال ثلاثة: الأول: البقية، واشتقاقه من: أثرث الشيء أثيره إثارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r7.claim: Al-Hasan takes athāra as a remaining portion of knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r7.anchor: الأول: البقية، واشتقاقه من: أثرث الشيء أثيره إثارة، كأنها بقية تستخرج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r8.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r8.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas's gloss: bring something you transmit from a prophet who preceded Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r8.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس؛ قال: يريد أو شيء ترويه عن نبي كان قبل محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r9.claim: Muqatil says it means a report from prophets that God has a partner; he attributes this view to Mujahid, Ikrima, and al-Qurazi.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أو رواية من علم عن الأنبياء أن لله شريكا (¬5)، وقال: هذا قول مجاهد وعكرمة والقرظي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r10.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r10.claim: In al-Kalbi's narration, athāra means a remnant of knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r10.anchor: وقال في رواية الكلبي: بقية من علم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r11.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r11.claim: Qatada explains it as special knowledge, perhaps a remnant preserved among learned specialists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p159#7/r11.anchor: وعلى هذا معنى قول قتادة: خاصة من العلم؛ لأن الخاصة من العلم بقية منه بقيت عند خواص العلماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r1.speaker: السلمي والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r1.claim: Al-Sulami and al-Hasan read athara with a different vocalization, supporting a sense of knowledge held exclusively by its possessor; al-Wahidi calls this a good interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r1.anchor: ويؤكد ما قلناه قراءة السلمي والحسن (أو أثرة من علم) (¬3)، والمعنى على هذا: ائتوني بعلم تنفردون به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi glosses athara or athāra as exclusive privilege; saying someone has athara in something means that person has a special claim to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r2.anchor: ويقال لفلان: أثرة بكذا أو أثارة، أي اختصاص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r3.speaker: أبو سلمة عن ابن عباس والشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r3.claim: Abu Salama reports from Ibn Abbas and al-Shaʿbi that athāra means knowledge of drawing lines in the earth, a divinatory practice of the Arabs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r3.anchor: وروى أبو سلمة (¬4) عن ابن عباس والشعبي أيضا عنه في قوله: {أو أثارة من علم} قال: هو علم الخط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r4.claim: The Prophet reports that a prophet used to draw lines; whoever's line matches his would know that prophet's knowledge, challenging the idolaters to produce such evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p162/r4.anchor: وروي عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أنه قال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r1.claim: Athāra means a remnant of knowledge inherited from the ancients.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r1.anchor: بقية من علم تؤثر عن الأولين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r2.claim: An alternative reading is athara, a noun on the faʿla pattern; the first reading athāra follows faʿāla.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p407#2/r2.anchor: ويقرأ: (أثرة) (3) ؛ اسم مبني على "فعلة" من ذلك. والأول على "فعالة".

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r4.claim: The challenge asks what the idols created on earth or whether they shared with God in creating the heavens and earth, which could justify worshipping them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r4.anchor: أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السموات } أي: مشاركة مع الله في خلقهما لذلك أشركتموهم في عبادته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r5.claim: They are challenged to bring a pre-Quran book that supports their claim.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r5.anchor: ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا } [أي: من قبل] القرآن فيه بيان ما تقولون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r6.claim: Atharah means a transmitted report from earlier prophets that they commanded worship of other than God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r6.anchor: رواية عن الأنبياء أنهم أمروا بعبادة غير الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r7.claim: Once the proof is established, God declares the idolaters the most astray.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:2-4/r7.anchor: فلما قامت عليهم الحجة جعلهم أضل الخلق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r1.claim: In common speech, “he showed me the stars by day” means that someone severely distressed or afflicted the speaker.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r1.anchor: والعامة تقول: أراني فلان الكواكب بالنهار، إذا برح به.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r2.speaker: الأعشى
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s phrase about seeing stars in daylight depicts someone returning sad and exhausted, as though daylight had darkened and stars gleamed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p108/r2.anchor: وقال الأعشى : رجعت لما رمت مستحسرا ... ترى للكواكب ظهرا وبيصا

ELMALILI:46:1-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:1-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:1-8/r1.claim: Athāra min ʿilm may mean a remnant of knowledge, transmitted knowledge inherited from earlier prophets, or writing traced on dust.
ELMALILI:46:1-8/r1.anchor: İlimden bakıyye kalmış bir eser, evvelki peygamberlerin ilimlerinden kalma me’sur bir ilim, yahut toz üstüne bir yazı.

MAJAZ:v2p212/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p212/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p212/r1.claim: Mā is used here with a collective, plural sense.
MAJAZ:v2p212/r1.anchor: «أرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض» (4) «ما» هاهنا فى موضع جميع

MAJAZ:v2p212/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p212/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p212/r2.claim: Athāra means a remnant; the camel-herder’s verse uses it for the remaining fat on which something has fed.
MAJAZ:v2p212/r2.anchor: «أو أثارة من علم» (4) أي بقية وقال راعى الإبل:

MAJAZ:v2p212/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p212/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p212/r3.claim: The form athara is analyzed as the verbal noun of atharahu yaʾthuruhu, ‘to mention or recount.’
MAJAZ:v2p212/r3.anchor: ومن قال أثرة فهو مصدر أثره يأثره يذكره

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r1.claim: The Qur'an's logic is that changing or affecting something requires participation in its creation; since idols created nothing, they have no basis for influence over it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r1.anchor: Birinin bir şey üzerinde değiştirici etkisinin bulunabilmesi için onun yaratılış ve oluşuna katkıda bulunmuş olma ön şartı vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r2.claim: Because people cannot see what occurs in the heavens, the verse states the idols have no share there as a thought-provoking question rather than saying, “show it if they do.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r2.anchor: “varsa gösterin” denilmemiş, yalnızca “etkilerinin olmadığı” düşündürücü bir soru şeklinde ortaya konmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r3.claim: Claims require rational and learned evidence or sound transmitted reports; the polytheists could provide neither the requested rational proof nor a reliable written or oral report.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:4/r3.anchor: Müşriklerden, önce akıl delili istenmiş, arkasından da sağlam bir yazılı veya yazısız rivayet talebi ile yetinilmiştir

ITQAN:v4p529/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p529/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p529/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet glossed athārah min ʿilm as handwriting or a written line; no grading is stated.
ITQAN:v4p529/r1.anchor: أخرج أحمد عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ أو أثارة من علم ﴾ قال ( الخط )

DAMGHANI:v1p442/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p442/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p442/r4.claim: من can mean في, 'in'; the example in 2:223 refers to the place God commands, identified as the vagina.
DAMGHANI:v1p442/r4.anchor: الثالث:من بمعنى فى.قوله تعالى فى سورة القرة

BURHAN:v4p419/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r11.claim: Min can mean fī, as in the call on Friday and asking what creatures made from the earth, or it can introduce a genus.
BURHAN:v4p419/r11.anchor: العاشر بمعنى في نحو ﴿ إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة ﴾

NASHR:v2p168/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p168/r2.claim: Readers agree to quiesce nine possessive yāʾs, including Yusuf's يدعونني إليه; some attribute this to the weight of many consecutive letters, while the source notes other explanations too.
NASHR:v2p168/r2.anchor: (واتفقوا) على: إسكان تسع ياءات من هذا الفصل، وهي في الأعراف أنظرني إلى
